hero.title: Secondary market for shares and incentive plan units
hero.description: Sttok gives shareholders a platform to buy and sell shares or incentive plan units. It only works if the company’s directors switch it on, and they decide whether offers are made only by the company or by the shareholders too. Sttok does not arrange the sales: it is the software where offers are published, participants are validated with KYC and contracts are signed. It is an add-on module.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about the secondary market

items.q: What is the Sttok secondary market?
items.a: A software platform where the company and, if it so decides, its shareholders publish buy and sell offers on shares or incentive plan units. Sttok does not arrange or broker the sales.

Only those the company authorises. The market is switched off until the directors switch it on, and they decide whether offers are made only by the company or by the shareholders too. Third parties have no access.
Anyone interested in an offer says so on the platform, participants are validated with KYC and the contracts are signed and accepted there. The deal is then entered in the shareholder register.

items.q: Does it work for incentive plans?
items.a: Yes. The company can make offers to buy vested units from plan beneficiaries, as liquidity windows.

items.q: Is it included in the plans?
items.a: No. It is an add-on module on top of any plan.

items.q: Does it work for companies in Latin America?
items.a: The platform adapts to each country's terminology: shareholder ledger, general shareholders' meeting, board of directors. Compliance with each country's regulations is assessed case by case.

situations.title: Common situations in the secondary market

rows.situation: The company wants to give shareholders or beneficiaries liquidity
rows.action: It switches the market on for itself only and publishes a buy offer with price, number of shares or units and deadline.
If the company opens the market to shareholders, they publish a sell offer and interested shareholders say so.

rows.situation: The articles provide for a right of first refusal
rows.action: The transfer remains subject to the notices and deadlines set in the articles.
Participants go through KYC, sign the contracts on the platform and the deal is entered in the shareholder register.
